title: Validate CI identifiers before authenticated URL and CLI construction
description:
## Finding

CI operations accept unvalidated string identifiers and interpolate them into authenticated provider URLs or CLI option positions. A typed run/job/ref operation can become a different request.

GitLab list adds a branch as raw `&ref={branch}`; legitimate Git refs can contain `&`, `=`, `%`, or `#`, changing query/fragment semantics. Project encoding only replaces slashes, while run/job IDs are inserted directly into path strings for read and mutation endpoints. GitHub places run IDs and workflow names in positional argv without canonical validation or an option terminator.

## Evidence

At `299fc13ee53f31bdeb99bbf35609a6ad55528973`:

* `crates/thegn-svc/src/ci.rs:562-565,583-585,596-611,642-649`: slash-only project encoding, raw branch query, raw run/job path components.
* `crates/thegn-svc/src/ci.rs:362,381,393,401`: caller strings in gh positional slots before/alongside flags.
* `crates/thegn-svc/src/ci.rs::id_str`: provider IDs accept arbitrary strings or any JSON number and are not validated before later reuse.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/cmd/ci.rs`: run/job/workflow arguments are unvalidated String fields.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/daemon/service.rs:1315-1397`: control API accepts run/job strings and forwards them to provider calls without canonical parsing.

A concrete harmless fixture is branch `feature&status=success`: current GitLab construction filters `ref=feature` and adds a status parameter. A run ID like `--help` changes gh interpretation and can produce a success exit without the requested mutation. These are argv/URL confusion, not shell interpolation; shell quoting does not fix them.

## Required remediation

Introduce provider-specific typed run/job/project/workflow identifiers at ingress and revalidate remote/cache values before reuse. GitHub/GitLab numeric IDs must have one canonical bounded integer grammar; workflow selectors may use a distinct supported name/path grammar. Validate branch/ref syntax independently and encode with a structured query builder.

Parse Git remotes as actual SSH/URL authorities and paths. Encode each URL component for its role, reject ambiguous double-encoding/traversal/control forms, and assert the final request retains the authorized origin/project/operation. Use a CLI option terminator where supported, with options placed before it; validation remains mandatory.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Valid branch refs containing query-reserved characters round-trip as one ref parameter.
- [ ] Run/job IDs with signs, decimal/exponent notation, leading option syntax, separators, dot segments, encoded delimiters, fragments, controls, or excessive length fail before any authenticated call.
- [ ] Legitimate workflow selectors are preserved without becoming flags.
- [ ] IDs read from provider JSON and caches use the same validator.
- [ ] Tests cover every CLI/control/provider entry and assert exact argv/URL plus zero requests for rejected inputs.
- [ ] No mutation can report success because gh printed help or entered another mode.
- [ ] No real provider mutation is used in tests.

## Dependency mapping

* No implementation prerequisite; canonical parsing and pure command-builder tests can be established independently.
* Blocks THE-539 (truthful mutation semantics require an unambiguous target).
* Related to THE-322 (same problem in tracker providers), THE-172 (control URL encoding), THE-538 (bounded CI execution), THE-114 (CI API/autofix consumer). None is a prerequisite.
